observed_failure: The rail stayed visible, but a first tab selection could take roughly 0.7 to 7.2 seconds to settle because the selected endpoint had not completed yet.
root_cause: The dominant delay was the first server and network response. A user click also cancelled speculative work and restarted the same request, so useful in-flight work was discarded.

hypotheses.evidence: Endpoint timing aligned with visible settle time while the client rail and loading state appeared immediately.
The rail did not disappear and the long wait tracked data completion rather than paint or transition duration.
The client can safely reuse one already-running request, warm the closest choices sequentially, and retain the existing bounded recovery path.

causal_change: Start bounded background priming after 800 ms instead of waiting five seconds.
Use one module-level serial queue so background work never creates a burst across the two rails.
Adopt the exact in-flight prime promise on selection instead of aborting and restarting it.
Bound the adopted wait by the remaining selection recovery budget so speculative work cannot prolong a click.
Skip speculative priming for hidden pages, Save-Data, 2G and slow-2G connections.
preserved_invariants: No supplier truth, identity, availability, price, ordering or image semantics changed.
No cache TTL, database, environment, DNS or scheduled job changed.
Late responses remain unable to overwrite a newer selection.
The existing visible rail, loading feedback and bounded recovery behavior remain active.
